extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners, patent practitioners, and other stakeholders interested in subject matter eligibility under 35 U.S.C. 101
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and supporting materials for USPTO examiners (and the public) on formulating subject matter eligibility rejections under 35 U.S.C. 101 and evaluating applicants' responses, including life-science examples, a decisions appendix, and a case-studies pilot to improve consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formulating a subject matter eligibility rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance to examiners on how to formulate a subject matter eligibility rejection under 35 U.S.C. 101.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The USPTO issued a memorandum titled 'Formulating a Subject Matter Eligibility Rejection and Evaluating the Applicant’s Response to a Subject Matter Eligibility Rejection' to improve examiner correspondence. The guidance sets out examination policy on rejections with respect to the Office’s interpretation of the subject matter eligibility requirements of 35 U.S.C. 101 in view of decisions by the U.S. Supreme Court and the Federal Circuit. Rejections will continue to be based upon the substantive law, and it is these rejections that are appealable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluating an applicant's response to an eligibility rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for examiners to evaluate the applicant’s response to a subject matter eligibility rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The memorandum provides guidance to examiners on evaluating a response to a subject matter eligibility rejection, with the objective of improving examiner correspondence. The guidance is internal examination policy and does not itself create enforceable rights; examiners should evaluate responses in light of substantive law and applicable case precedent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Life science examples for eligibility analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of life-science example claims and hypothetical scenarios as teaching tools for applying eligibility guidance in fact-specific situations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The USPTO produced new life science examples that provide exemplary subject matter eligibility analysis under 35 U.S.C. 101 of hypothetical claims and claims drawn from case law. The examples are intended as a teaching tool to assist examiners and the public in understanding how the Office would apply the eligibility guidance in certain fact-specific situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix 3: chart of select eligibility decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: A curated chart of Supreme Court and Federal Circuit decisions to assist examiners in identifying types of subject matter courts have found ineligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appendix 3 contains select eligibility decisions from the Supreme Court and the Federal Circuit and will continue to be updated with Federal Circuit decisions having opinions (precedential or non-precedential). Non-precedential decisions provide guidance and persuasive reasoning as outlined in Fed. Cir. R. 32.1(d). Appendix 3 will also be updated with Federal Circuit decisions without opinion (Fed. Cir. R. 36) on appeals originating from the Patent Trial and Appeal Board. Federal Circuit decisions affirming a district court decision without opinion (Fed. Cir. R. 36) will no longer be added to Appendix 3 because they provide little benefit to examiners or the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance materials are non-binding internal policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarification that the USPTO guidance materials do not constitute substantive rulemaking and do not have the force and effect of law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guidance materials set out examination policy and were developed as a matter of internal Office management; they are not intended to create any right or benefit, substantive or procedural, enforceable by any party against the Office. Failure of Office personnel to follow the USPTO’s guidance materials is not, in itself, a proper basis for either an appeal or a petition. Rejections remain based on substantive law and are appealable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case Studies Pilot Program to review consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: A program to study and improve consistency of subject matter eligibility analyses across the examining corps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The USPTO solicited topics for the Topic Submission for Case Studies Pilot Program. The case studies will include a review of consistency of the application of subject matter eligibility analyses under 35 U.S.C. 101 across the examining corps to determine the quality of the work product and indicate where improvements can be made to further improve consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public comment solicitation and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Open-ended solicitation for public comments on the July 2015 Update, the examiner memorandum, life science examples, and progress on correspondence quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The comment period is open-ended and comments will be accepted on an ongoing basis; when the period will close, advance notification will be made. Comments should be submitted electronically (plain text preferred; PDFs and Word accepted) to the provided email; comments will be publicly available so submitters should avoid including information they do not wish made public (e.g., addresses, phone numbers, CBI). The USPTO is particularly interested in comments addressing the progress the USPTO is making in the quality of correspondence regarding subject matter eligibility rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of precedential and persuasive decisions in examiner analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on which court decisions are included and how examiners should treat precedential vs. non-precedential opinions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appendix 3 will be updated with Federal Circuit decisions having opinions (precedential or non-precedential); while non-precedential decisions are not binding precedent, the opinions provide guidance and persuasive reasoning per Fed. Cir. R. 32.1(d). The guidance explains inclusion/exclusion rules for Fed. Cir. R.36 decisions and that certain affirmances without opinion provide little benefit and are no longer added.
